sub_questions.text_english: Explain the following points of importance of delegation : (i) Employee development (ii) Motivation of employees (iii) Effective management

key_points: Employee development: delegation provides subordinates with challenging tasks that build skills and prepare them for higher responsibilities
Motivation: being trusted with authority gives employees recognition, boosting morale and job satisfaction
Effective management: delegation frees managers from routine tasks, allowing them to focus on strategic decisions

sub_questions.solution: Delegation is important for the following three reasons. First, it aids in employee development. When managers delegate tasks to subordinates, they give them an opportunity to work on challenging assignments that go beyond their routine duties. This hands-on experience helps subordinates learn new skills, develop their decision-making abilities, and gain confidence. Over time, they become capable of handling greater responsibilities, which builds a pipeline of competent future managers within the organisation and reduces the risk of managerial succession gaps. Second, delegation serves as a means of motivation for employees. When a superior delegates authority to a subordinate, it is an expression of trust and confidence in the subordinate's abilities. This recognition of their potential acts as a powerful motivator — employees feel valued and important, which boosts their morale, commitment, and job satisfaction. Motivated employees tend to perform at a higher level and show greater loyalty to the organisation. Third, delegation enables effective management. A manager's time and energy are limited. If a manager tries to handle every task personally, they will be overwhelmed with routine work and unable to concentrate on strategic, high-value decisions. Delegation allows managers to transfer routine tasks to capable subordinates, freeing the manager to focus on planning, policy-making, and other critical functions that require senior-level judgement, thereby making the entire management process more efficient and effective.

sub_questions.text: नियोजन के महत्त्व के निम्नलिखित बिन्दुओं को समझाइए : (i) नियोजन निर्देशन की व्यवस्था करता है (ii) नियोजन अतिव्यापित तथा अपव्ययी क्रियाओं को कम करता है (iii) नियोजन नियंत्रण के मानकों का निर्धारण करता है
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the following points of importance of planning : (i) Planning provides directions (ii) Planning reduces overlapping and wasteful activities (iii) Planning establishes standards for controlling

key_points: Provides directions: planning gives employees a clear sense of where the organisation is headed
Reduces wasteful activities: coordinated plans prevent duplication and pointless efforts
Establishes standards for controlling: pre-set targets act as benchmarks against which actual performance is measured

sub_questions.solution: Planning is important for the following three reasons. First, planning provides directions. Planning sets out clearly defined objectives and outlines the course of action to be followed by the entire organisation. This gives all managers and employees a sense of direction — they know where the organisation is headed, what their specific role is, and how their individual efforts contribute to the larger goal. Without planning, all decisions and actions would be fragmented and uncoordinated, leading to chaos. Second, planning reduces overlapping and wasteful activities. When plans are prepared in advance and communicated to all departments, everyone understands their responsibilities and the sequence of activities required. This prevents two departments from unknowingly doing the same work and avoids situations where time, money, and effort are spent on activities that do not contribute to organisational goals. Coordinated plans thus promote efficiency and eliminate unnecessary duplication of effort. Third, planning establishes standards for controlling. Planning and controlling are inseparable functions — planning sets the targets and controlling checks whether those targets have been achieved. Without a pre-defined standard or benchmark, there is nothing to compare actual performance against. Planning establishes these benchmarks — such as production targets, sales quotas, and cost budgets — which then serve as reference points for measuring and evaluating actual performance, identifying deviations, and taking corrective action.
